title: Petra and the Sigil
premise: Lior Iversen, exiled to the magic-dead valley of Hollowmere for a storm-calling she barely remembers committing, has built a quiet life of small deceptions—until a date with a charming stranger, Petra, appears verbatim in a century-old prophecy book. The prophecy names Petra as the Sigil-bearer whose awakening will reignite the war between the storm-crowned houses and the valley's founders, and it names Lior as the one who must kill her. Torn between love and duty, Lior discovers her exile was engineered by the founders to keep her—the true living sigil's key—from ever meeting Petra; when Petra awakens and the founders move to execute her, Lior breaks the valley's ban on magic, calling a storm that shatters both prophecy and the founders' power, choosing an unwritten future with Petra over the safety of invisibility.
about_author: August Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing banned grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people trapped by histories they never chose.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Establishes Hollowmere, where magic dies at the ridge line, and Lior's careful, small life as a bookbinder. She tends a hidden scar on her palm that aches when storms pass beyond the hills. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: A Stranger Orders Tea
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Petra arrives in town, charming and oddly curious about Lior's work restoring old books. Their first conversation sparks something Lior hasn't felt in years. Emotional beat: cautious hope, the terror of being noticed.

chapters.title: The Date
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Their first proper evening together—a lantern-lit walk, shared confidences, a kiss under rain that never crosses the ridge. Lior feels seen for the first time since exile. Emotional beat: joy shadowed by instinctive dread.

chapters.title: Ink Older Than Memory
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Restoring a donated volume, Lior finds a prophecy book written a century ago—and reads tonight's date, the teahouse, the rain, the kiss, word for word. Emotional beat: vertigo, the ground of her life dissolving.

chapters.title: What the Page Promises
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, with flashback fragments. The prophecy continues: the Sigil-bearer will wake, and the Key must end her before the war reignites. Lior realizes she is named—not by name, but by her scar. Emotional beat: horror curdling into denial.

chapters.title: Petra, Unremarkable and Impossible
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. We see Petra's own secrets: she came to Hollowmere deliberately, following dreams of a valley and a woman with a scarred hand. Emotional beat: longing entangled with guilt over what she hasn't told Lior.

chapters.title: Second Meeting, First Lie
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior meets Petra again, testing her against the prophecy's details while hiding what she knows. Every true thing Petra says tightens the trap. Emotional beat: the corruption of intimacy by secrecy.

chapters.title: The Warden of Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The valley's warden, Maren, notices Lior's agitation and reveals a sliver of truth: the founders sealed magic out to starve someone specific. Lior learns her exile was arranged, not sentenced. Emotional beat: betrayal reframing her whole past.

chapters.title: Dreams of the Storm-Crown
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra's dreams intensify—she sees the war, the storm-crowned houses, and a figure calling lightning with Lior's face. She wakes with a mark blooming on her collarbone. Emotional beat: fear of becoming something chosen by others.

chapters.title: Confessions in the Bookbindery
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating scenes. Lior shows Petra the prophecy; Petra admits she sought her out. Neither can say what the prophecy demands of them. Emotional beat: love declared in the same breath as doom.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Breaking into the warden's archive, Lior finds the founders' records: her childhood trial was staged, her memory altered, because she alone can unlock or destroy the Sigil. Emotional beat: rage at a life stolen to serve a design.

chapters.title: Marked
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The mark spreads; Petra begins hearing the valley's dead founders whispering instructions. She hides it from Lior, mirroring Lior's earlier lie. Emotional beat: power arriving like an infection.

chapters.title: Maren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Warden Maren offers a deal: kill Petra quietly, and Lior regains her freedom and name. She gives Lior three days. Emotional beat: duty weaponized against love.

chapters.title: Three Days
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Lior and Petra spend the countdown together, half-lovers, half-strangers, each aware time is ending. Tender, aching domesticity against the ticking clock. Emotional beat: love sharpened by imminent loss.

chapters.title: The Ridge Line
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior tries to smuggle Petra out before the deadline, but the valley's boundary burns Petra back—the Sigil cannot leave until it wakes or dies. Emotional beat: desperation meeting an unbreakable wall.

chapters.title: Awakening
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Cornered by Maren's wardens, Petra's mark ignites; the Sigil wakes, and the dead founders speak through her mouth, demanding the war be refought. Emotional beat: selfhood drowning in borrowed purpose.

chapters.title: The Key Turns
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior confronts Petra-as-Sigil and understands at last: the prophecy needs her consent. Refusing both options—kill or obey—she cuts her scarred palm on the archive's iron and claims her role as Key on her own terms. Emotional beat: agency seized from fate.

chapters.title: Storm Over Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, rapid cuts. Lior calls the storm she was exiled for, breaking the valley's ban; magic floods back as Petra fights the founders from within. The two powers meet in the sky above the town. Emotional beat: cathartic, terrifying release.

chapters.title: What the Prophecy Got Wrong
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In the storm's eye, Lior reaches Petra and speaks her real name—not the Sigil's—and the founders' grip shatters. The prophecy book burns itself blank. Emotional beat: love as an act of refusal.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Weather
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The valley wakes changed: magic present but unruled, the founders gone, Maren stripped of office. Petra grieves what the Sigil did through her and doubts what remains of her. Emotional beat: raw, uncertain recovery.

chapters.title: Names We Choose
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior formally renounces her restored title, choosing exile-turned-home; she and Petra rebuild the bookbindery together, writing a new ledger with no prophecies in it. Emotional beat: quiet reconciliation with identity.

chapters.title: Rain That Crosses the Ridge
chapters.summary: Dual closing POV. A year later, rain falls freely over Hollowmere for the first time in a century. Lior and Petra walk beneath it, unprophesied and unafraid. Final image: a blank page waiting. Emotional beat: earned peace, open future.
